summary:
Mission Relics is an educational web-based encyclopedia that introduces school-age students and curious space enthusiasts to the robotic explorers and scientific equipment left behind by humanity's space missions. It focuses on hardware across the Moon, Mars, and other destinations, explaining what each piece of equipment was designed to do, which mission carried it, and how it contributed to scientific exploration.

Instead of presenting space hardware as a collection of technical facts, Mission Relics organizes information into accessible articles that connect each artifact to its mission and scientific purpose. It aims to make the history of space exploration easier to discover, understand, and appreciate.

By bringing attention to both active and inactive space hardware, Mission Relics helps younger audiences explore the engineering achievements and scientific legacy of past missions and inspires curiosity about future exploration.
details:
How it works


Mission Relics is a web-based educational encyclopedia. Visitors can explore articles about space exploration hardware, discover the missions associated with each artifact, learn about its purpose and destination, and understand the scientific work it helped make possible. Each article presents information in an accessible format and includes references for further reading.

Purpose and intended impact


The project responds to the challenge of making the history of abandoned and inactive space hardware more engaging and accessible to school-age audiences. Many historical mission records are technical and difficult for beginners to explore. Mission Relics brings these stories together in one educational experience, helping visitors understand that even equipment no longer operating can leave an important scientific legacy.

Tools and development


The website was developed using Google AI Studio and web-based development tools. Publicly available space-mission information and NASA resources were used to research, verify, and organize the educational content.

AI tools supported different stages of development: Google Gemini assisted with research and organizing information, Google AI Studio supported AI-assisted website development, and ChatGPT (GPT) assisted with writing, prompt creation, planning, and development guidance. The project concept, direction, selection of featured hardware, and final decisions were independently guided by the creator.

Creative approach

Rather than focusing only on currently active missions, Mission Relics highlights the historical equipment that made earlier exploration possible. It connects individual pieces of hardware to their missions, purposes, and scientific contributions, giving visitors a way to explore the history behind space exploration. To make learning more interactive, each article also includes an optional question-and-answer section at the end, allowing readers to test their understanding of what they have learned and reinforce key information.
